item.title: Italy Participates in Singapore International Cyber Week 2026
item.description:
(ANSA) - ROMA, 16 OTT - Promoting Italian expertise in the cybersecurity sector and deepening the dialogue on emerging challenges in cyber diplomacy were the objectives of the visit to Singapore, from October 14 to 16, by Minister Plenipotentiary Alessandro De Pedys, Director General for Cyber Affairs, Information Technology, and Technological Innovation at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, on the occasion of the Singapore International Cyber Week (SICW) 2026. The Italian pavilion at SICW—one of the leading international events dedicated to cybersecurity, promoted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Farnesina) in collaboration with the Italian Trade Agency (ICE) and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN)—brought together eight Italian companies interested in developing new business opportunities and partnerships in Singapore and Southeast Asia. As part of the event, De Pedys participated in the panel discussion “Italy’s Experience in Strengthening the National Cybersecurity Ecosystem,” alongside Luca Nicoletti of the ACN and Sergio Strozzi of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which focused on Italy’s experience in strengthening the national cybersecurity ecosystem. Italy’s contribution to the international debate continued during the fair’s high-level sessions on diplomacy, with De Pedys participating in the panel “Algorithms and Alliances: Will AI Take Over Cyber Diplomacy?”, which focused on the impact of artificial intelligence on cyber diplomacy and the new challenges for international relations. The mission included meetings with representatives of Singaporean institutions and participation in the sixth edition of the Counter Ransomware Initiative, aimed at strengthening international coordination against ransomware attacks and addressing new threats linked to technological advancements. Rounding out the program was De Pedys’ participation in a roundtable discussion on strategic communication and combating disinformation, hosted by Italian Ambassador Dante Brandi at the embassy, as well as a visit to the “Abito” exhibition, held at the National Gallery Singapore and presented abroad for the first time, which explores the dialogue between fashion, architecture, and interior design as an expression of Italian creativity.

item.title: Italy and Mozambique Strengthen Early Warning System in Sofala
item.description:
(ANSA) - BEIRA, 16 OTT - The new Situation Room at the Sofala Province Emergency Operations Center was inaugurated today in Beira. It is designed to strengthen the capacity to predict and respond to cyclones, floods, and other extreme events in a region that was severely affected by Cyclone Idai in 2019. The ceremony was attended by the Italian Ambassador to Mozambique, Gabriele Annis; the President of the National Institute for Risk and Disaster Management (INGD), Luisa Meque; and Foreign Minister Manuela Lucas. Sofala has become the first province in Mozambique to have a Situation Room integrated with the national system and linked to the continental architecture of the African Multi-Hazard Early Warning and Early Action System (AMHEWAS), promoted by the African Union. The facility is one of the outcomes of the Ready2Act project, implemented with the support of Italian Cooperation and technical contributions from the Cima Foundation, the Italian Department of Civil Protection, and the NGO WeWorld. Over the course of more than two years, the project has strengthened Mozambique’s monitoring, forecasting, and response capabilities through technology transfer, technical training, and the exchange of expertise. This Situation Room complements the one at the National Emergency Operations Center (CENOE) in Maputo, which was inaugurated in September 2025. “Today we are inaugurating a control room, but above all, we are strengthening a network,” emphasized Luca Ferraris, president of the Cima Foundation. For Annis, the initiative “confirms the value of collaboration with Italy in transforming the ability to anticipate risks into concrete actions to protect people and communities.”

item.title: Meloni urges opposition to condemn violence at student protests
item.description:
(ANSA) - ROME, 16 OTT - Premier Giorgia Meloni on Friday called on the opposition to condemn the violence at anti-government student protests across Italy earlier in the day. High-school students urging more cash for schools and less for arms threw rocks and firecrackers at police in Rome, Turin and other cities. Regarding the student protests, "I am always pleased when there is mobilization. But violence—such as the use of homemade explosive devices or attacks on law enforcement—is a different matter. We must be clear and in agreement on this. I say this because I am looking at the comments from opposition leaders regarding the protests, and they have failed to utter a single word of condemnation. I call on all Italian political forces to urge that demonstrations take place without violence." Speaking after the European Council in Brussels, Meloni called on opposition parties to be "clear" on this issue. (ANSA).
